notes: Literature-derived Suzuki-Miyaura condition map with expanded substrate classes, emphasizing catalyst-base-solvent pairings and stability guidance.

Aryl_Halides.title: Aryl Halide Electrophiles
Aryl_Halides.description: Tuning ligation state and base strength for aryl iodides, bromides, chlorides, and triflates.

electrophile_scope: aryl bromides without severe steric hindrance
entries.operational_notes: Maintain an equimolar Pd to phosphine ratio to favor mono-ligated Pd(0) that accelerates transmetallation.
entries.scope_limitations: Electron-poor chlorides and strongly coordinating heterocycles need more donating ligands or stronger bases.

supporting_evidence.quote: Thus, fastest transmetallation was observed with one equivalent of a more electron deficient mono-phosphine ligand consistent with transmetallation being the rate determining step.
A combination of Pd(PPh3)4 or PdCl2(PPh3)2 and aqueous Na2CO3 in dimethoxyethane works satisfactorily in most cases.

entries.operational_notes: Bulky biaryl ligands enforce mono-ligation and create a pocket that accommodates ortho substituents.
entries.scope_limitations: Extreme steric clash or acid-sensitive substituents may require lower base strength or alternative ligands.

supporting_evidence.quote: The Buchwald group developed an exceptional Pd catalyst for the Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling of challenging aryl halides. An electron-rich biaryl ligand 95 was designed to provide the necessary steric interactions and electron density.
Employing this ligand, cross-coupling between sterically hindered aryl halides and aryl boronic acids or alkylboranes was accomplished with low catalyst loadings.

entries.operational_notes: Use strongly donating, bulky ligands to accelerate oxidative addition into C-Cl and ensure adequate base strength for boronate activation.
entries.scope_limitations: Coordinating heterocycles can slow oxidative addition; additives such as fluoride may be required when protodeboronation competes.

supporting_evidence.quote: Chlorobenzene derivatives are generally quite inert to oxidative addition, but some pi-difficient heteroaryl chlorides give coupling products.

entries.operational_notes: Electron-rich biaryl ligands balance steric bulk and donor capacity to push oxidative addition of unactivated C-Cl bonds.
entries.scope_limitations: When base-sensitive groups are present, swap to milder phosphate or carbonate salts and consider lower temperature.

supporting_evidence.quote: Employing this ligand, cross-coupling between sterically hindered aryl halides and aryl boronic acids or alkylboranes was accomplished with low catalyst loadings.

entries.operational_notes: Powdered K3PO4 in aprotic solvent efficiently promotes triflate couplings; boronic acids outperform esters for arylations.
entries.scope_limitations: Moisture accelerates hydrolysis of activated triflates; exclude water unless using slow-release boron sources.

supporting_evidence.quote: Powdered K3PO4 suspended in THF or dioxane is sufficient to accelerate the coupling of 9-alkyl-9-BBN, 1-alkenyl-, and arylboronates or boronic acids with triflates.

Heteroaryl_Substrates.title: Heteroaryl Electrophiles and Boron Partners
Heteroaryl_Substrates.description: Mitigating protodeboronation and coordination for N- and O-containing heterocycles.

entries.operational_notes: Combine rapid-activation precatalysts, copper additives, masking ligands, and slow-release hydrolysis to keep free boronic acid levels low.
entries.scope_limitations: Excess water accelerates MIDA hydrolysis beyond control; maintain biphasic solvent ratios and add base gradually.

supporting_evidence.quote: A precatalyst was employed that undergoes rapid activation to directly form a highly active mono-coordinated XPhos-ligated palladium(0) complex.
The 2-pyridyl MIDA boronate steadily hydrolyses throughout the coupling, reducing exposure of the liberated boronic acid to protodeboronation.

catalytic_systems.system_name: Pd(PPh3)4 in THF with aqueous base

entries.operational_notes: Air-stable diethyl boranes simplify handling; phase-transfer salts keep the boronate engaged in biphasic media.
entries.scope_limitations: Hydrolytic deboronation increases under fully aqueous conditions; retain an organic co-solvent.

supporting_evidence.quote: Diethyl(3-pyridyl)borane synthesized by Terashima is a unique air-stable reagent for heteroarylation.

entries.substrate_class: Thiophene and furan derivatives susceptible to protodeboronation
entries.operational_notes: Preformed lithium triisopropylboronates resist protodeboronation and remain active after extended storage.
entries.scope_limitations: Limited solubility in nonpolar solvents; include minor water fractions or polar co-solvents for activation.

supporting_evidence.quote: Lithium triisopropylboronates are stabilized by Lewis-base coordination and are more resistant to protodeboronation than regular boronic acids, especially for 2-heteroaryl substrates.

entries.operational_notes: Strong, bulky alkoxide bases generate the active boronate required for transmetallation; potassium cations stabilize the transition state.
entries.scope_limitations: Sodium or lithium tert-butoxide fail to form the reactive boronate; maintain strict exclusion of moisture.

supporting_evidence.quote: Only potassium tert-butanolate and not the corresponding sodium or lithium base promoted formation of the boronate required for transmetallation.

Vinyl_and_Alkenyl.title: Vinyl and Alkenyl Electrophiles
Vinyl_and_Alkenyl.description: Protecting stereochemistry in C(sp2)-C(sp2) alkenyl couplings.

entries.operational_notes: Run at room temperature with acetate base to suppress cis/trans isomerization during coupling.
entries.scope_limitations: More basic media trigger beta-elimination; avoid strong bases with sensitive vinyl halides.

supporting_evidence.quote: PdCl2(dppf) is effective for carrying out the reaction at room temperature in order to depress isomerization during the coupling.

Alkyl_sp3.title: Alkyl C(sp3) Couplings
Alkyl_sp3.description: Addressing beta-hydride elimination and stereochemical drift in alkyl Suzuki-Miyaura reactions.

entries.operational_notes: Hydroboration followed by Suzuki coupling furnishes 1,4-dienes and allylbenzenes with controlled branched-to-linear ratios.
entries.scope_limitations: Pd(PPh3)4 can deactivate in very polar media; keep a biphasic organic layer to maintain catalyst activity.

supporting_evidence.quote: Hydroboration of alkynes with disiamylborane, followed by cross-coupling with allylic or benzylic halides in the presence of Pd(PPh3)4 and aqueous NaOH produces 1,4-alkadienes or allylbenzenes in high yields.

entries.operational_notes: Triphenylphosphine-bound palladium minimizes beta-hydride elimination when run at 60 °C with excess phosphate base.
entries.scope_limitations: Bidentate phosphines slow reductive elimination; avoid dppe, dppp, or dppb for these substrates.

supporting_evidence.quote: The palladium complex with triphenylphosphine as ligand is recognized to be most effective for cross-coupling between 9-alkyl-9-BBN and primary iodoalkanes.

entries.operational_notes: Silver(I) additives scavenge halide and promote transmetallation, allowing retention of stereochemistry at room temperature.
entries.scope_limitations: Coordinating functional groups on the alkyl fragment can trigger inversion; maintain inert atmosphere and exclude protic impurities.

supporting_evidence.quote: Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling of chiral secondary alkylboronic esters with aryl iodides in the presence of Pd2(dba)3 and Ag2O afforded products in high yields with retention of configuration.

Boron_Strategy_and_Stability.title: Boron Source Selection and Stability
Boron_Strategy_and_Stability.description: Choosing boron reagents, masking groups, and borylation strategies to manage protodeboronation and reactivity.

entries.substrate_class: General boronic acids across pH windows
entries.operational_notes: Adjust pH to the plateau region of the boronate stability curve; neutral electron-rich arenes remain stable above their pKa whereas 2-pyridyl boronates demand masking or pH control.
entries.scope_limitations: 3,4-pyrazolyl and 3,4-oxazolyl boronates become labile at higher pH; unmasked 2-pyridyl boronates can degrade under strongly basic conditions.

supporting_evidence.quote: Protodeboronation rates of various boronic acid substrates can vary by over seven orders of magnitude between substrates at the same pH as well as across the pH range.

entries.operational_notes: Pd-catalysed borylation furnishes boronic esters in one step, providing modular access to downstream Suzuki couplings.
entries.scope_limitations: Hydride-sensitive functional groups may undergo reduction; consider lower temperatures or alternative bases.

supporting_evidence.quote: The palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling of (alkoxy)diboron derivatives provides a one-step procedure for arylboronic esters from aryl halides.

Process_and_Sustainability.title: Process-Friendly and Green Protocols
Process_and_Sustainability.description: Lowering precious metal loadings and solvent impact while preserving reactivity.

entries.substrate_class: Aryl halides with micellar Ni catalysis
entries.operational_notes: Designer surfactant TPGS-750-M retains the catalyst in water, enabling low organic solvent usage and facile product extraction.
entries.scope_limitations: Hydrophobic substrates may require small co-solvent charges; maintain surfactant concentration to avoid deactivation.

supporting_evidence.quote: They used a designer surfactant TPGS-750-M engineered to remain in the water phase during in-flask extraction, requiring minimal organic solvent.
